pr_title: ref(crons): Reorganize incident creation / issue occurrence logic

validations.droid_claim:
[P1] Incident can trigger before reaching failure_issue_threshold

When `failure_issue_threshold > 1`, the code slices up to `failure_issue_threshold` check-ins but never verifies it actually retrieved that many; if a new monitor has fewer total check-ins than the threshold and all are failures, `any(status==OK)` will be false and an incident will be created prematurely. Add a guard like `if len(previous_checkins) < failure_issue_threshold: return False` before creating the incident.
validations.impact: A new monitor with fewer check-ins than failure_issue_threshold will trigger an incident prematurely if all existing check-ins are failures, even though the threshold count has not been reached.
validations.reasoning: In incidents.py lines 38-55, when failure_issue_threshold > 1 the code queries check-ins, slices to [:failure_issue_threshold], then checks if any have status OK. If a monitor has only 1-2 check-ins but threshold is e.g. 3, the slice returns fewer items than the threshold. Since all returned check-ins are failures, the any(OK) check is False and execution proceeds to create the incident. There is no guard verifying len(previous_checkins) >= failure_issue_threshold before proceeding.
validations.code_evidence:
Lines 38-55:
previous_checkins = cast(
    list[SimpleCheckIn],
    MonitorCheckIn.objects.filter(
        monitor_environment=monitor_env, date_added__lte=failed_checkin.date_added
    )
    .order_by("-date_added")
    .values("id", "date_added", "status"),
)
previous_checkins = list(reversed(previous_checkins[:failure_issue_threshold]))
if any([checkin["status"] == CheckInStatus.OK for checkin in previous_checkins]):
    return False
# No check that len(previous_checkins) == failure_issue_threshold

validations.droid_claim:
[P1] get_monitor_environment_context returns unmodified config

This function copies `monitor_environment.monitor.config` into `config` and updates `config["schedule_type"]`, but then returns `"config": monitor_environment.monitor.config` (the original) instead of the local `config`. As a result, the schedule_type display transformation never takes effect in the emitted context.
validations.impact: The schedule_type display transformation in the monitor context is silently dropped. The occurrence event data will contain the raw schedule_type integer instead of the human-readable display string.
validations.reasoning: In incident_occurrence.py lines 161-173, the function creates a local copy `config = monitor_environment.monitor.config.copy()`, modifies `config["schedule_type"]` to the display value, but then returns `"config": monitor_environment.monitor.config` (the original unmodified config) instead of `"config": config`. The local copy with the display transformation is discarded.
